findings.finding: The source location initially called the receivables sheet physical page 3 even though the actual PDF places printed page 5 at zero-based index 3, physical page 4.
findings.resolution: Author changed the source verification to printed page 5 (PDF index 3; physical page 4). Reviewer inspected both the actual primary body and final corrected record. Method scope and chapter arithmetic were unaffected.

reasoning_audit.recognition: The chapter supplies valid delivered/accepted goods, fixed prices and unconditional receivables before using the sales ledger. It distinguishes advances, pro forma billing without an enforceable right, later credit losses and contractual price changes. No blanket invoice-date or doubtful-collection recognition rule is inferred.
reasoning_audit.allowance_and_recovery: G-Z is the asset carrying amount; the allowance is not cash or a liability. Writeoff reduces both gross and allowance without immediate net-asset change. Reinstatement has the same net-neutral property; subsequent collection moves an asset to cash. Final re-estimation may affect profit. The target stock and expense adjustment are distinguished, including negative expense and a debit pre-adjustment allowance. The lab transparently restricts recoveries to claims written off in the same period.
reasoning_audit.cash_identities: Derived customer cash S-dG+dU-W+H and supplier cash COGS+dI-dAP directly. The gross bridge includes both the expense addback and -W+H; the raw net bridge already incorporates allowance movements and requires no second expense addback. The higher-target counterexample correctly leaves cash invariant while reducing both profit and net N.
reasoning_audit.ratios: Stock/flow units are days with a common 90-day interval. Gross credit-sale DSO, net DSO, total-revenue DSO, credit-purchase DPO, total-purchase DPO and COGS-based DPO are distinctly labeled. Undefined zero-flow ratios propagate to dependent CCC. Mixed cash/credit activity, margins, endpoint averaging, growth, writeoffs and seasonality preclude an exact physical-delay claim.
reasoning_audit.pipeline: Under the supplied steady all-credit/no-loss deterministic-lag model, N=s*dR+c*(dI-dP), so N-c*CCC=(s-c)*dR. This proves that negative CCC can coexist with positive dollar financing needs. Changed steady stocks are not silently used as a full transition cash calendar.
reasoning_audit.calendar: Main journals are explicitly grouped quarter postings, with purchase-before-related-delivery stipulated and detailed dates/cost allocations unspecified. The separate cash-only calendar assumes receipts precede payments inside each bucket; it reports an infeasible unfinanced path and a conditional available zero-cost facility, not observed or guaranteed funding. Peak shortfall supplies a necessity bound and the exhibited draw/repayment path establishes sufficiency within those assumptions.
reasoning_audit.financing_choice: The supplier discount is compared at the same day-30 date against a feasible day-10-to-day-30 loan. Rate d/(1-d) uses the actual early amount financed; 360-day simple annualization is not called an effective compound return. Availability, repayment capacity and no additional fees/terms are stated.
reasoning_audit.code: Read all benchmark and checker lines. Integer minor-unit money and rational loss/day calculations avoid hidden rounding. Generated journal and nonnegative asset/liability bounds, full aging coverage, same-period recovery constraint and the separate calendar-total reconciliation are consistent with the documented bounded model. Validation uses explicit exceptions and remains active under optimization. Arithmetic consistency does not establish source-document completeness.

exercise_review.result: June cash +14, revenue 7, COGS 9/2, profit/equity +5/2, gross AR -1, inventory -9/2, advances +6; assets +17/2 = liabilities +6 plus equity +5/2. Pro forma invoice creates no entry under the supplied no-right condition.

Gross AR 55; target/expense 9/2; net AR 101/2; inventory 35, AP 30, advances 8; revenue 126, profit 83/2. Customer cash 119 and supplier cash 60 yield CFO 44 and cash 54. Closing assets 279/2 = liabilities 38 + equity 203/2. Gross N 54 to 52 and net N 50 to 95/2 each reconcile CFO 44.

Gross/allowance/net stages are (40,5,35), (37,2,35), (38,3,35), (37,3,34); the collection adds cash 1. Final target 4 requires expense 1 and leaves net AR 33. Without recovery, expense would be 2 at the same target; re-estimation carries the profit difference.

DSO 30, DIO 25, matched DPO 20, CCC 35 days. COGS DPO gives 15 and CCC 40; total-sales DSO gives 20 and CCC 25. Supplier settlement 160 plus cash purchases 80 equals total cash 240. No individual payment dates are identified.

Raw event cash [-60,40,-30,100,80], CFO 60, closing cash 80. Facility 60 is necessary at day 10 and sufficient via funded path [0,100,30,160,140], then repayment 60. Limit 40 leaves shortage 20. Accrual profit is not identified by this cash calendar.
Stocks AR 50, inventory 40, AP 70 imply N 20 and CCC -5. Scaling both daily flows by 3/2 yields 75,60,105 and N 30, requiring 10 more N. The margin identity gives 20-2*(-5)=30=(5-2)*10.

Loan interest 49/75, day-30 repayment 7399/75, saving versus face amount 101/75. Supplier credit costs 1/49 over 20 days; simple annual equivalent 18/49, greater than the stated 12% loan rate. Funding/contractual conditions are part of the comparison.
